beats.narration_en: Why did a steel wall just jump out of the road?
It's a security barrier. In an emergency it rises in about a second.
Under the road, a hinged steel plate waits inside a concrete pit.
Hydraulic pistons swing its front edge up, nearly three feet high.
A car that hits it doesn't just bounce off the steel.
Thick struts push the crash down into tons of buried concrete.
So the car stops dead, and its back end flips into the air.
Tested ones can stop a fifteen thousand pound truck going fifty.
That's what those striped steel plates at secure gates are for.
